name: Sea of Stars (adjacent: active turn combat)

pos.text:
Usually I don’t really write reviews, but this game is special. As a full time working dad my time is very limited. However, this game reignited the love that I felt for games in a period where time was available in abundance, and your time was respected by developers. Furthermore, it reminds me of a time where the world seemed more simple, and devs still cared about their art before shareholders and marketeers dictated the course of development of a game.

The game embraces old school jrpg vibes whilst it does not take itself too seriously. The characters are light hearted but serious when required during certain phases of story telling. I find them engaging and above all courageous. The overall story is quite simple but that is certainly not a bad thing, it’s well put together.

The combat system is simple but in depth enough to keep me hooked. The lock system is a clever way to ensure
[u]Spectacle[/u]

[b] Sea of Stars is a beautifully made RPG that brings together amazing pixel art, a memorable soundtrack, fun combat and a charming story to create a truly amazing adventure. Every part of the game feels carefully crafted, from its world and characters to its little details, making it an experience that every RPG fan should try.
P.S.: I don't think New Game+ has much to offer after completing the game, except if you missed 1 or 2 achievements. There are a couple of missables, so it can be useful for completionists.
P.S.2: There are items called Relics in the game that let you make the experience easier, harder or more comfortable for you.
P.S.3: My boy Garl 💪❤️ [/b]

I don't think a positive review is what this game really deserves, but it for sure is not thumbs down worthy.
I get what this game tries to do, but it falls short on every aspect, aside from the graphics, maybe.

Rpg elements are really barebones, stats are basic and have very little depth.
Dialogues and story feel pretty average, nothing stands out (Characters or events)
Combat is alright. Again, not much depth to it, but it compensates with good difficulty and quick time events such as parries and power ups.
Hated the backtracking.

In the end this is a very forgettable game which, however, you'll still enjoy playing. 6.5/10

What a phenomenal experience

Sea of Stars builds upon the already solid foundation that Sabotage established with The Messenger and adds a wonderful RPG journey through beautifully rendered worlds filled with fun NPCs, fantastic music and well thought out designs.

When I finally finished this game last night, I felt as if I'd just had a warm dessert, was tucked in and even got to say thank you to the devs themselves. This is a great game that will leave you feeling warm and fuzzy inside. There's a lot of fun to be had, the combat is very enjoyable and there's a lot to explore and do!

[b]Gameplay[/b]
Honestly great, I really liked the turn based combat, and the timed hits/blocks system makes it so battles have some agency beyond just picking the right moves at the right time, but that is the extent to where it goes, if you expect something like the Mario and Luigi series where you can actually dodge this isnt it, but it is solid enough for me to recommend it to you if you look for a experience close to it.

[b]Music[/b]
The music is good, with some standout pieces close to exceptional, there is no song in this game that I would describe as bad, and I thoroughly enjoyed listening to it alongside playing the game and the OST matched the Vibes closely

[b]Visuals[/b]
Really beautiful, thats literally how I feel, as someone born in the 2000's I wasn't around when Pixel Art was widespread, but I still have some fond Childhood memories of playing tloz: The Mini

This plays like a cousin to Chrono Trigger.  I've been having fun playing it, and reading the conversations to my little niece.  One of the few little kid friendly games I have I can play with her in the room.

It's polished, accommodating, accessible. The graphics are very expertly done, and the gameplay is well-tuned. It's a frictionless game, and I don't find much of it memorable. I prefer experiences with some rough edges, or with a more avant-garde style. In a world with DELTARUNE, or Hylics, or OFF!, it's not a stand-out product. But! It [i]is[/i] a good product. If you want a classic-style turn-based action RPG, it's worth the time and money. Just don't expect it to go against the grain.
It's a fun and nicely made game that bloats out in the second half and has an incredibly boring secret ending. Boring in getting to it. The secret ending itself is cool.

Sea of Stars is an absolute joy to play on the Steam Deck. The vibrant pixel art and gorgeous environments really pop on the OLED display, and the memorable soundtrack perfectly complements the world.

The combat is easy to pick up but has enough depth to keep encounters interesting. The story and characters aren’t anything groundbreaking, but they do their job well and kept me wanting to play.

The Relics are a nice touch too, letting you tweak specific mechanics to make the experience easier or harder to suit your preferences.

A fantastic game, especially for short portable sessions on the Deck. Highly recommend!

The world is expansive and the story is well done and I was very happy with the vintage style enemies and NPCs.  Plus the wheels mini games are goated.  I love games with mini games that I'm excited to play and incentivized to complete.  This game is 8/10 solo and 9.5/10 with friends with very minor gripes about how difficult the puzzles are. Honestly this game should be great, but it's just not. The lock system is meant to add decision to combat, but fails pretty bad and makes combat unfun and frustrating a lot of the time. Basically the way it works is that enemies will sometimes use strong attacks, but you get a turn to try to hit them with specific attack types to stop their attack from going off. That sounds good on paper, but it doesn't work as implemented:

* If you try to break locks, to usually have to save your abilities/empowered attacks to be able to do that in the number of turns provided. Enemies also take reduced damage while channeling locked abilities (60% reduced in my game). So you’re encouraged to save all your strongest damaging abilities for when enemies take the least damage, making fights a slow awful grind.

* Alternatively, ignore breaking locks, and save abilities for when enemies aren’t locked. Fin

Pros:
Phenomenal art and music and fantastic battle gameplay (minus the ants that summon more ants, which summon more ants... that's wildly bad design, especially in early game). If this game were just an endless dungeon crawler/rogue-like focused entirely on the combat mechanics, or even if it were mostly that with other gameplay, I would easily sink 100+ hours into it.

Issues:
The main protagonists have the combined charisma of a wet paper towel. 

Moving around to different areas on the map feels slow and pointless. 

The devs, for whatever reason, made Garl take over as the unplayable main character early in the game. He should have been a dog, honestly. 

It feels like if you and one other person work really hard on a group project and the third guy signs his name at the bottom, sneezes in your face, blesses himself, and then the teacher gives him extra credit for creativity. 

The
game is fun but the story never really gels and the ending was very unsatisfying

This game is the biggest bait in jrpg history.  It looks pretty but looks are deceiving.  The story goes nowhere for... literally the entire early game.  I've never seen such cool character concepts be so dull, and the combat has no variety at all.  I can appreciate well thought out simplicity, but after using moonerang for the 80th time...  And just when I thought the story might do something interesting, I was given a hand wave with the "power of friendship..." again...

Seriously, just go play Chrono Trigger.  This ain't it.  Or if you want to play something new, try out Chained Echoes.  It isn't perfect, but it at least dared to be creative.

Sea of Stars was a game that I had on my wishlist for a long time and was excited for, after hearing it was positioning itself as something of a spiritual successor to the JRPGs of my childhood, like Chrono Trigger, FFVI and Super Mario RPG. In some ways, it is. It certainly has the look and sound - the graphics, animations and music are excellent. After that, the game barely compares.
  
The battle system mostly combines Chrono Trigger's skill combos with Super Mario RPG's timed button press system, though characters don't learn nearly the variety of moves as in those games, so what you end up doing in the first hours of the game isn't far removed from what you're doing in the final hours. There's also a lock system - essentially a way to reduce or negate enemy spells by hitting them with the right combination of attacks - but I found that much of the time breaking the lock was either n
I wanted to love it. I played for more than 20 hours waiting for something interesting to happen, but unfortunately this game is boring, mainly because of writing, which is simply weak.

If you play the game in a straightforward way, clearing the story and be done, then its okayish.
If youre a completitionist and want to do all content, then its a piece of ♥♥♥♥.

Wheels is rigged like no other mini-game I've ever seen. The AI has access to triple tiles which you dont, levels up its figurine every other turn and clearly has the advantage in its "rng".
Some puzzles are simply annoyances more than mind breaking
Some optional bosses are just sponges with annoying mechanics.

Honestly Im about to simply cheat my way into getting all the achievements to be able to move away from this. 

There is some good though. The art style is great, the music as well. 
I would give it a middle thumb but since it does not exist, Ill go with a negative review because my expectations were not met for the most of it.

I really wanted to love this game. I tried and tried, booted it up again, left it, picked it up again multiple times. But I just cant play it. The visuals are amazing, the designs really cool, the music is both nostalgic and really good, the combat is fun and sometimes challenging, it has good QoL. So then, what is the problem with this game?

The writing. Its horrid. It makes visually appealing characters feel hollow and generic. It makes an interesting premise fail to hook the player's attention. It makes the world feel shallow. It makes the game go from a gem of its genre to a forgettable one.

And it frustrates me a lot, because it feels like they genuinely put so much love on this game, on every aspect of it... Except the writing. Would it have killed you to take a writing class? Did you try your best to make the story and dialogues as boring and empty as possible? I dont understand

The writers don't know how to write a video game. The story mostly wants to be taken seriously, but with lots of silly characters, and overall it doesn't work. MLSS sticks to its silliness and I like the story better.

The writing is simply bad. I cannot maintain my suspension of disbelief because the story is constantly introducing new, totally unrelated ideas without any unifying threads to tie them all together. Here's a simple example: "Songster Magic," which is used by a late-game character. To my recollection, it is only mentioned once in the story. It has no ties to the rest of the world and is seemingly only put in place because the designers wanted singing magic. This, plus the gods that shall not be named, the rules that powerfu

reviews.title: Great port, please add 1-handed support
reviews.text: I adore this game & played it on steam. Quickly bought the port and am adoring it. Very elegant controls. My one request would be to allow either side of the screen to be touched in order to select/dragged to use the d-pad; regardless of what side of the screen you touch. I know many other mobile ports that allow for this. Or perhaps a way to switch sides in the menu? I recently suffered a hand injury and cannot play video games with a regular controller until I heal. I am so grateful I can play SoS on mobile now, as it is actually a platform I can play video games on while my arm is injured. But it would be so much easier for me if I didn’t have to reach across either side of the screen every time I wanted to move/talk/jump/attack. A small inconvenience that I can handle, but it would surely increase accessibility for me and for many others with more permanent limb differences. Thank yo

reviews.title: A Worthwhile RPG
reviews.text:
I checked the online reviews before deciding to shell out the $8 for this. So far, it’s lived up to the positive reviews. 

The graphics are colorful and surprisingly well detailed. Done in what I’d say is reminiscent of 32-bit pixel games, but the level of shading and environmental animations bring a depth to the world. 

The story and characters are your standard JRPG fare, but if you’re into these games that’s not a negative, it’s just saying that part isn’t new or extra creative.

I had trouble at first figuring out what the battle instructions meant when saying to hold a particular button to enhance the attack, because the icon doesn’t look like any visible buttons on the screen, then I realized it meant to just press and hold the screen. It’s more obvious on the male character’s sun ball attack than on the female character’s Luna attacks. And blocking to reduce damage seems more ch

reviews.title: The game you’ve been waiting for
reviews.text:
First off, I have played so many iPhone games it’s pretty crazy… as a busy dad who loves games I don’t really have time for gaming systems and have become an iPhone game enthusiast and this game has knocked it out of the park!

I grew up obsessed with final fantasy and was pretty stoked that playdigious was putting this out there and wanted to give this a try and it has not disappointed! 

This mobile RPG feels like it was built from the ground up with the spirit of classic fantasy epics in mind, while embracing gameplay on an iPhone

At its core, the game delivers a beautifully balanced turn-based combat system that never feels stale. Every decision matters, but what really sets it apart is the clever layer of bonus mechanics woven into each action. Timed inputs that can make or break a battle keep the fights interesting and you have to pay attention… SERIOUSLY LOVE IT! and the game has

reviews.title: Love this game!!
reviews.text: Original I had bought this on my Switch and loved it so much that I figured I’d buy it on my phone as well since I never take my Switch with me. The only reason I’m giving the version 4 starts is because there is 0 graphics controls and my iPhone 16 pro max  is better than my Switch and the Switch version looked better. Second the game needs more quick saves because there has been a few times where I left the game closed for too long only to come back and lose 30-45 minutes of work.. but still highly recommend this game. One of the better stories to come out as of late.

reviews.title: A MUST have. Trust me and Purchase it
reviews.text: I’m not one to leave many reviews. I think last time I left a review was for Nexomon: Extinction. Just like that one, I have to leave a review because both share some characteristics you cannot help but love. You can tell when developers love their work. I was so impressed with characters who were not stale. They didn’t leave everything to gameplay to carry the game. They gave you art, a great world design that’s beautiful and my favorite was the plot with characters you Loved! Have way into the game, I found myself dreading the moment when I’d get to the end. Surprisingly it was longer than expected so I was able to relish the time until that last mission. Guys - trust me. You will love this game. There’s humor, a refreshing take to old fashion designs and I cannot wait for the studios next installment. I heard there’s a DLC? Please bring it to IOS.

reviews.title: Incredible adventure, well made port
reviews.text:
This is a must play for any RPG fans. It has a great story (especially if you’ve played The Messenger). The combat system is incredibly satisfying, be it through perfectly timed hits, or the strategic options that live mana opens up. 

As for the port itself, the touch controls feel very natural. You’re never required to hold more than one button at once (movement circle not counting as a button), so you don’t have to hold the phone awkwardly. There’s controller support too, so you can use the original controls. My only gripe is that I wish you could switch the confirm/cancel buttons on a controller layout. It’s not really an issue, since I can just change that in the phone settings, but it’d be nice I could do it in a way that didn’t also change the button labels.

reviews.title: Smooth, Polished, and Fun
reviews.text:
Sea of Stars has been an absolute joy so far. About five hours in, and it already feels like a love letter to classics like Chrono Trigger and Super Mario RPG, two of my all-time favorites. The combat, exploration, and overall vibe hit that same nostalgic sweet spot while still feeling fresh.

The humor lands, the music is fantastic, and everything just comes together in a really polished way. I’ve also been especially impressed with the Relics system, which lets you tailor the difficulty to your preference. Some make the game more forgiving (like automatically healing after battles so you don’t have to constantly manage menus), while others add extra challenge. It’s a great approach that makes the game more accessible without taking away from the core experience.

The mobile version itself is very well done. The touch controls feel natural and responsive, and I haven’t experienced any i

reviews.title: Controls and saving
reviews.text: Game is amazing 10/10. But you need to be able to touch anywhere on the screen to move the characters. Left and right half of the screen don’t work on this type of game. Even if you make an option to swap it that won’t solve the problem. It’s an easy fix that the devs absolutely can do with little effort. This is the main issue but also you need to make the game auto save all the time. In a game like this you easily lose a half hour of playtime if you get interrupted because the game closes if minimized even briefly. Anyway this is one of my favorite games and the 3rd time I’ve bought it, so please please fix these extremely minor yet extremely major qol issues. Love you guys

reviews.title: Must have game.
reviews.text: Never heard of Sea of Stars until it showed up on upcoming games section. I was hesitant to spend money on a pre-order. But once I opened it up and played for 5 min I knew it was 100% worth.  Absolutely amazing game. Music makes this game. Characters are great. Combat is enjoyable and interactive. Only thing I could think of while playing this is “man I wish I could play this Co-op”.  After some research I now know that was a DLC the original game had before being ported for Mobile. Let’s hope the Devs see our love for this game and bring the DLC to Mobile! I’m here for it!  10/10 game for me!

reviews.title: Wonderful, except one bug
reviews.text:
As someone who doesn't game very much, I'm enjoying this. Graphics are beautiful, storyline is enjoyable and challenging without being tedious or repetitive. Overall a very good game. 

My only complaint is I can only play in-game audio. Almost every other app/game I have used gives me the option to play external music/audio books while playing the game, as I don't always want to listen to the game music, but this overrides any audio besides the games, even if the in game volume is all the way down or the phones silent mode is on/off.

reviews.title: Cool Port; Aspect Ratio Shortcoming
reviews.text: A great RPG and generally a well done port by Playdigious. One issue for me, though, and I bring it up here only because the game’s product page doesn’t: the aspect ratio presented here is a severely letterboxed version on iPad (and I assume iPhone too, although to a lesser degree). There’s been no attempt to provide an option to reframe or zoom visuals to fit the aspect ratio of your device. As long as you’re okay with less gameplay real estate, the game is still great. But hopefully 1) they address this; and 2) they clearly let buyers know what they are and are not getting.

reviews.title: Pre-Ordered the hell out of it
reviews.text: And it did not disappoint oh my god. The graphics, the art style, the fluid animation, the combat, the relic features that give players more customization and accessibility, and the music. All peak. But the UI for settings is a bit clunky, you have to click around too much just to get 5 items to adjust, and aside from settings, when you try to skip a cutscene, the game takes a second to register both fingers before loading the next scene. Otherwise, aside from these two issues, amazing game.

reviews.title: Generational game
reviews.text: Everything about this is perfect. It translates perfectly to a game played on a phone. I only have one complaint/suggestion. Since it is being played on a phone, which means I play it on the go and in spurts, I would love an option that skips all of the intro title screens and immediately goes to continue my game. On top of that, an option to enable saves from anywhere. I can’t always play long enough to get to a save point and the game will close in the background, requiring a re-play of sections.

reviews.title: Amazing RPG, one frustrating issue
reviews.text: This game is just incredible really! Very reminiscent of Chrono Trigger and a very engaging story. One issue I have run into that has caused me to lose progress and almost be softlocked is a graphical glitch that freezes the screen makes it impossible to navigate or battle. It seems to happen only when lots of rendering power is needed, but it completely ruins the game and halts progress until you’re lucky enough to somehow make it past the problem areas. Hopefully this can be fixed cause it truly is a great game.

reviews.title: So much lost progress
reviews.text: It’s a wonderful game that’s extremely well crafted. But that’s not the reason I’m writing this review. I’ve just completed what I need to do for the red crystal (it’s for the pirates quest) and whenever I leave the round thing colorful static comes up and the game freezes. And it’s honestly horrible. Because it happens every time and always after I finish the level. I have no idea why it’s happening, but it’s really killing the mood.

reviews.title: Excellent Game, Missing Content
reviews.text: The game is excellent. It captures the feel of the games that inspired it like Chrono Trigger while still doing new things so it’s not just a boring retread of successful ideas. It seems to be missing the Throes of the Watchmaker scenario despite otherwise being on par with the pc and console release. It’s unclear if there is an issue keeping it from starting or if it’s not part of the mobile release but the latter seems unlikely in light of how it otherwise matches other versions. Either way it needs to be addressed.

The only thing I wish there was is a quicksave feature.

reviews.title: Obra maestra del Pixelart
reviews.text:
Sea of Stars es uno de los mejores juegos Pixelart que he jugado nunca.

El juego se siente vivo, te envuelven sus escenarios con el arte, los colores y la iluminación. Un detalle “tonto” que me sorprendió y habla muy bien del nivel de detalle es que en una cueva habían unas columnas verdes de cristal, al pasar por detrás los personajes no solo se difuminaron sutilmente, también se distorsionó su forma y se iluminaron del mismo color, tal como sucede con el vidrio. Lo que hicieron con pixeles me parece imposible de superar…

Además la historia es increíble, nunca sabes qué esperar en la próxima misión y tiene bastante contenido. Llevo ya 22h de juego pero creo que no he superado ni el 50% de la historia.

Y la música, la música es INCREIBLE. Súbanle el volumen al máximo porque se lo merece. Recuerdo entrar a la Isla Espectral, ir a la taberna del pueblo, y quedarme como 15 min escuchando

reviews.title: Just buy it! (First time player)
reviews.text:
Gorgeous graphics, fun and easy to follow story. It’s my first time and I found myself just stopping to admire the scenery honestly. It’s flipping beautiful. It just feels cozy. Only an hour in, but I can guarantee that $9 is BEYOND well worth. ALSO, major thanks to the crazy cool coders working on this game- they fixed a soft lock bug EXTREMELY fast (<1day). This is a company that listens to their fans, fixes bugs, and doesn’t waste time. Love, love. Take my money. Take my damn heart atp. 

PS: I know there are mixed reviews for this game generally. People say the characters are 1D (no personality), the writing is bad, the story is generic or unfulfilling. My two cents? Well, Im not done, I just started, but I can see some of these critiques; HOWEVER, I dont agree. My opinion: why cant we just have a fun story with simple writing, big moments, and light hearted characters who dont talk
